text:
maria: quick follow-up from the attention-quant RFC — we need to lock down kernel routing and dequant fallback policy before the next rollout. can we fuse dequant into attention kernels safely? what are the memory/latency tradeoffs? cc @kevin @sam @olga

kevin: short answer: yes we can fuse, but there are two modes: in-place streaming dequant (low mem copy, higher compute complexity) vs batch dequant to FP16/FP32 then run existing kernels (simpler, more mem).

sam: memory is the big win for fused path. if we dequant on-the-fly into regs/SM-managed memory we skip writing big FP buffers for QKV. that reduces bandwidth and helps tail latency. downside: much more complex kernels and fragile per-arch tuning. :thinking:

olga: one safety concern: softmax stability and accumulation precision. if we do int8/FP8->FP16 inside kernel, we must accumulate softmax in FP32 or scaled FP16 with proper headwise scaling. otherwise we get numeric regressions. we should add evals that compare per-head KL/ROUGE on our standard eval sets.

kevin: agreed. proposal: fused_dequant_attn kernel variants do dequant->accum in FP32 internally, keep per-head scale as input. signature idea:

```
// simplified pseudo-signature
__global__ void fused_attn_dequant_qkv(const int8_t* qkv_packed, const float* scales, float* out, int B, int H, int S);
```

kevin: note scales could be per-tensor, per-channel (per-head), or per-row. API needs to support all three but we should default to per-head for best quality/size tradeoff.

maria: what about KV cache format? we currently store cached keys/values as FP16 tensors. if fused kernel avoids materializing FP16 QKV it would need to write into KV cache — can we write quantized+scale and dequant only on read? or must we materialize FP16 KV for downstream non-fused kernels?

sam: interesting idea — store KV as (int8, scale) tuples in cache. pros: less memory. cons: many existing kernels assume FP16 cache layout. would require a compatibility layer that can present either view. runtime could advertise cache_format: [fp16|packed_int8].

olga: that compatibility layer sounds like a good long-term plan but big refactor. short-term we should implement forced materialization on write for non-fused consumers, and add an opt-in packed cache for Dedicated/private customers.

maria: fallback policy question: if fused kernel is available for model+seq_len+device, great. else fallback to non-fused FP16 kernels. do we also allow a mid-path: dequant->FP16 host-side and run existing kernels? i.e., a temporary fallback that avoids float kernels?

kevin: yes, we should have a routing priority list: 1) fused_attn_dequant (preferred), 2) device-side dequant+FP16 kernel (dequant kernel then call existing FP16 attn), 3) native FP16 attn. This lets us gradually enable fused kernels in canary.

maria: rollout plan? metrics to watch?

sam: canary with small percent of traffic, synthetic perf harness for p50/p95/tail and per-model quality regression tests. track: token throughput, GPU mem usage, bandwidth (GB/s), and per-head KL/QA/ROUGE deltas. Add a fallback threshold: if p95 latency > baseline*1.2 or quality delta > epsilon then auto-roll back that canary cohort.

olga: also add a correctness checklist: deterministic numerics for same seed, no NaNs/inf, and reproducible softmax outputs within tolerance. unit tests: random QKV fuzz with golden FP32 reference.

kevin: microbench results from local prototype: fused path reduces memory writes by ~40% and improves p99 by ~12% for seq_len=2048, batch=4 on A100. startup overhead is higher (kernel compile and larger register use), so less wins at tiny seq lengths.

maria: good. action items:
- kevin: prepare a kernel API RFC with signatures for fused and dequant kernels (include scale formats). due EOW.
- sam: prototype packed KV cache layout and a small compatibility shim. due next week.
- olga: define eval thresholds and add tests to ci-evals. due EOW.
- infra-bot: schedule canary job for fused kernels once kevin's RFC lands.

infra-bot: noted. canary job will be queued when the rfc PR is merged. CI: perf-harness will run 10k tokens per variant by default. :gear:

maria: one more question on quant formats: FP8 variants (E4M3 vs E5M2) — we should pick a canonical FP8 internal representation for fused kernels or accept multiple?

kevin: probably accept both but require the quantization metadata (exp bias, format id) passed into kernel. easier to be generic than to bake assumptions. small cost to branch on format at kernel entry.

sam: final note: document expected mem layout in agents docs and create a migration guide for customers who rely on raw KV layout. otherwise a private deployment could break on upgrade.

maria: thanks — I'll gather these into a short RFC follow-up and tag the eng-runtime release PR. :shipit:
